hooks.text: A structure 100 times wider than the Milky Way is technically average.
Why would an ordinary galaxy create a structure 16 million light-years wide?
The universe's largest galactic structure was blown by an average galaxy.

title: The Ordinary Galaxy 100 Times Wider than the Milky Way
description: Meet Alcyoneus, a colossal radio galaxy spanning 16 million light-years across the cosmic web.

beats.text: A structure 100 times wider than the Milky Way is technically average.
beats.visual: artist concept of a giant radio galaxy with massive glowing lobes

beats.text: In 2022, astronomers used the LOFAR radio network to discover Alcyoneus, a record-shattering giant.
beats.visual: photograph of the LOFAR antenna array in the Netherlands

beats.text: Over three billion light-years away, this radio galaxy spans at least 16 million light-years.
beats.visual: radio optical overlay of Alcyoneus galaxy showing massive plumes

beats.text: That is equivalent to laying over one hundred Milky Ways end-to-end.
beats.visual: infographic showing a row of spiral galaxies comparing Milky Way scale

beats.text: If our eyes saw radio waves, these lobes would look as large as the moon.
beats.visual: composite image of the full moon next to a radio galaxy to scale

beats.text: Twin plasma jets launched from the core near light speed to inflate this gargantuan structure.
beats.visual: artist concept of relativistic jets emerging from a black hole core
queries: supermassive black hole relativistic jet illustration

beats.text: Researchers expected a monster black hole, but found an average host with no star birth.
beats.visual: Hubble image of a quiet elliptical galaxy in deep space

beats.text: It grew this massive because it sits in a lonely, empty pocket of the cosmic web.
beats.visual: computer simulation showing the large scale structure of the cosmic web

beats.text: This cosmic titan exists only because it was blown by an ordinary galaxy.
beats.visual: side-by-side comparison of the host galaxy point and the radio lobes

better_than_last: Eliminated discovery dates and specific author names mid-script to focus purely on the physics and scale, accelerating the reveal as per the proven rule from ep030.
